hypothesis: Aggregating 4 independent RAG drafts via embedding-cluster consensus should surface decision-critical unknowns (which recur across samples) and suppress niche/redundant ones — providing a new criticality signal beyond exp002's self-rated importance or exp004's keyword scoring.
technique: Four independent RAG-prompted on-device drafts are drawn at temperatures [0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0], producing 28 candidate questions; NLEmbedding cosine clustering (merge threshold ≥ 0.62, greedy) collapses near-duplicates, then the 7 clusters with the broadest cross-sample agreement (distinct-sample count, tiebroken by avg position) are kept, each represented by its centroid-nearest member — all deterministic Swift post-processing after the model calls.
result: Scored 0.222 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), a sharp drop of −0.098 below the exp003 best (0.320) and −0.085 below baseline. Coverage collapsed to 2: embedding clustering failed to merge question paraphrases (cosine too coarse), so near-duplicate pairs survived, and cross-sample frequency surfaced generic filler ("any additional factors?") rather than sharp task-specific unknowns — confirming the 3B's modal output is the generic one and that aggregating more of its own samples cannot recover Sonnet-level judgment. Discarded.
label: exp010
